title: Beyond Repair: Killing Your Job
coreMove: Use strategic quitting only after repair fails: define the protected life, price staying, lower exit risk, then leave if the job still blocks it.

exampleSpecs.audience: an associate weighing a partner-track offer
exampleSpecs.stakes: A respected title may preserve a deferred life instead of buying usable freedom.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the prestige career and 80-hour weeks to expose a sunk-cost stay.

exampleSpecs.audience: a project lead preparing a possible resignation
exampleSpecs.stakes: Leaving without runway may turn a rational exit into panic.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use runway, savings, side income, and muse to reduce transition danger.

exampleSpecs.audience: a product manager comparing resignation with repair
exampleSpecs.stakes: Emotion may hide both quitting risks and staying costs.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use fear-setting to compare exit damage with the cost of staying.

exampleSpecs.audience: a department chair considering a return to consulting
exampleSpecs.stakes: Past investment may be mistaken for future fit.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use sunk cost and deferred life to challenge the prestige career pull.

exampleSpecs.audience: a general manager with a small outside business
exampleSpecs.stakes: A side project can lower risk without becoming a fantasy cure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use savings, side income, runway, and muse as exit supports.

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations director deciding whether negotiation has failed
exampleSpecs.stakes: Vague frustration could force a premature exit or an endless stay.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Make repair failure explicit before treating the role as beyond repair.
